_what: Hand-written notes about bills whose number carries a standing meaning. Edited by a person; no generator writes this file, and preflight fails if one tries.
_why_two_sections: Some bills are the same thing under the same number every term -- HB1 is the budget in nineteen of them. Others are the same thing under a DIFFERENT number every term: the ten-year transportation plan is HB2000, then HB2004, HB2006, HB2010, and so on to HB2026. One key shape cannot hold both, so there are two, and neither can be mistaken for the {term: {bill: ...}} shape the rest of this project uses.

_fields.from: every_term only. The first TERM the note is true of. Earlier bills of that number are different bills that happen to share it.
_fields.until: every_term only, optional. The last term it is true of, where a convention has ended.
_fields.label: A short name for the bill's standing role, shown as a heading.
_fields.note: The explanation, in Granite Record's own words. The page says so: this is not the General Court speaking.
_fields.checked: When a person last read it and agreed with it.

_verified: HB1 exists from 1989-1990 but is not the budget until 1993-1994: the 1989 bill is a special session bill on public utilities commission approval and the 1991 bill is a medicaid enhancement tax. The appropriations title runs unbroken from 1993 to 2025, exactly alongside HB2. Without 'from', this file would publish a false statement on two terms from the day it shipped.

HB1.label: The state budget
HB1.note: HB 1 is the core financial spreadsheet of the state budget, filed alongside HB 2 in the first year of the term. It outlines the exact line-item spending for public services, healthcare, infrastructure, and state agencies for a two-year period.

HB2.label: The budget trailer bill
HB2.note: HB 2 is known as the budget trailer bill, filed alongside HB 1 in the first year of the term. Because HB 1 only specifies monetary amounts, HB 2 contains the statutory law changes, fee adjustments, and policy language needed to execute and pay for that spending. HB 2 can make changes to state tax structures, raise or lower state fees, and update funding formulas. HB 2 may also contain policy items not directly related to the budget through amendments.
